## Time Series
<hr>

Lines for time series, w/ time on the x-axis

Look for:

trends, seasonal patterns, cyclical patterns, noise

missing values, outliers, sudden changes

## Mortgage data
<hr>

```{r data}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
theme_set(theme_linedraw(16))
url <- "https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/historicalweeklydata.xlsx"
# download.file(url, "historicalweeklydata.xlsx", mode = "wb")
df <- read_excel("historicalweeklydata.xlsx", skip = 7,
                 col_names = c("DATE", "30 YR FIXED", "fees1", "15 YR FIXED", "fees2",
                               "5/1 ARM", "fees3", "margin", "spread"),
                 col_types = c("date", rep("numeric", 8)),
                 na = c("", " ")) |>
  filter(!is.na(DATE)) |>
  select(DATE, `30 YR FIXED`, `15 YR FIXED`, `5/1 ARM`) |>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE))
head(df)
```


## Transform data

```{r pivot}
df <- df |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = -DATE, names_to = "TYPE", values_to = "RATE",
               values_drop_na = TRUE) |> 
  mutate(TYPE = forcats::fct_reorder2(TYPE, DATE, RATE)) # puts legend in correct order
head(df)
```

## Multiple time series

```{r mortgagepres}
ggplot(df, aes(DATE, RATE, color = TYPE)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "U.S. Mortgage Rates", x = "", y = "percent") +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
```


## No. 😭
<hr>

```{r mortgage}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(df, aes(DATE, RATE, fill = TYPE)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "U.S. Mortgage Rates")
```

## Filter
<hr>

```{r}
library(lubridate)
df |>
  filter(year(DATE) >= 2020 & year(DATE) <= 2021) |> 
  ggplot(aes(DATE, RATE, color = TYPE)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "U.S. Mortgage Rates")
```

## What is the overall long-term trend (secular)?
<hr>

```{r}
# data from https://www.boxofficemojo.com/release/rl226461185/
dfman <- read_csv("ManchesterByTheSea.csv")
g <- ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Manchester by the Sea", subtitle = "Daily Gross (US$), United States", x = "2016-2017")
g
```

## Loess smoother (non-parametric)
<hr>

```{r loess}
#| echo: false
dfman$Group <- round(1:nrow(dfman)/(nrow(dfman)/6))
g <- ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) +
  geom_point()
g +
  geom_line(color = "grey50") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, lwd =1.5, span = .5) +
  labs(title = "Loess smoother")
```

## Loess smoother (conceptual idea)
<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: false
g +
  geom_line(color = "grey50") +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = Group), method = 'lm', color = "red", se = FALSE)
```

## Under / overfitting
<hr>

<img src="loesscrop.png" width = "400" />

<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: true

```

##

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# with weekly summary
weekly <- dfman |>
    group_by(Year = year(Date),
             Week = week(Date)) |>
    summarize(AvgWeeklyGross = mean(Gross)) |>
    mutate(Date = as.Date("2015-12-27") +
               365*(Year - 2016) +
               7*(Week -1))
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross/1000000)) +
    geom_line(color = "grey30") +
    geom_line(data = weekly,
              aes(Date, AvgWeeklyGross/1000000),
              color = "blue", lwd = 1.5) +
    geom_smooth(color = "deeppink", lwd = 1.5,
                se = FALSE) +
    annotate("text", x = as.Date("2017-02-15"),
             y = 1.65, label = "average weekly gross",
             color = "blue", hjust = 0) +
    annotate("segment", x = as.Date("2017-02-01"),
             xend = as.Date("2017-02-12"), y = 1.65,
             yend = 1.65, color = "blue", lwd = 1.5) +
    annotate("text", x = as.Date("2017-02-15"),
             y = 1.5, label = "geom_smooth()",
             color = "deeppink", hjust = 0) +
    annotate("segment", x = as.Date("2017-02-01"),
             xend = as.Date("2017-02-12"), y = 1.5,
             yend = 1.5, color = "deeppink", lwd = 1.5) +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b\n%Y") +
    labs(title = "Manchester by the Sea",
         subtitle = "Daily Gross, United States", 
         x = NULL, 
         y = ("Daily Box Office Gross \n (in millions US$)"))
```


## Seasonal trends
<hr>

```{r}
ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) + geom_line()
```

## Are there seasonal patterns?
<hr>

```{r}
ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) + geom_line() + geom_point()
```

##

```{r}
library(plotly)
p <- plot_ly(
    dfman, x = ~Date, y = ~Gross,
    type = 'scatter',
    mode = 'lines+markers',
    # Hover text:
    hoverinfo = 'text',
    text = ~paste(Day)
)
p
```

## Mark the pattern
<hr>

```{r}
g <- ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) + geom_line() +
    labs(title = "Manchester by the Sea",
         subtitle = "Daily Gross, United States")
saturday <- dfman |> filter(wday(Date) == 7)
g + geom_point(data = saturday, aes(Date, Gross),
               color = "deeppink")
```


## Facet to test (remove) seasonal pattern
<hr>

```{r, fig.height = 6}
# facets
ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_grid(wday(Date, label = TRUE)~.)
```

## Another view
<hr>

```{r facetbyday}
#| fig-width: 9
ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) +
    geom_line(color = "grey30") + geom_point(size = 1) +
    facet_grid(.~wday(Date, label = TRUE)) +
    theme_linedraw()
```

## With smoother
<hr>

```{r facetbydaysmooth}
#| fig-width: 9
ggplot(dfman, aes(Date, Gross)) +
    geom_line(color = "grey30") + geom_point(size = 1) +
    facet_grid(.~wday(Date, label = TRUE)) +
    geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
    theme_linedraw()
```

## Cyclical or seasonal?
<hr>

```{r}
# Data from ggplot2 package
econ <- economics |>
  select(date, unemploy, pop) |>
  mutate(unemploy_rate = unemploy / pop * 100)

econplot <- econ |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = unemploy_rate)) + geom_line() +
  labs(title = "U.S. Unemployment Rate", x = "Date", y = "Percent Unemployed")
econplot
```

## Trend

```{r}
econplot + geom_smooth(aes(color = "Loess, span = .75"), span = .75, se = FALSE) + # default span
  labs(title = "U.S. Unemployment Rate") +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Smoother", values = c("blue")) + 
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```


## Trend and cyclical components
<hr>

```{r}
econ_cycle <- econ |> mutate(trend = predict(loess(unemploy_rate ~ as.numeric(date)))) |>
  mutate(cycle = unemploy_rate - trend) |> 
  pivot_longer(c(unemploy_rate, trend, cycle), names_to = "component", values_to = "value")
ggplot(econ_cycle, aes(x = date, y = value)) + geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~fct_rev(component), ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate: Trend and Cyclical Components", x = "Date", y = "Percent") 
```

## What's wrong?
<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: false
econ_cycle <- econ |> mutate(trend = predict(loess(unemploy_rate ~ as.numeric(date), span = .2))) |>
  mutate(cycle = unemploy_rate - trend) |> 
  pivot_longer(c(unemploy_rate, trend, cycle), names_to = "component", values_to = "value")

ggplot(econ_cycle, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~fct_rev(component), ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate: Trend and Cyclical Components", x = "Date", y = "Percent")
```

## What's wrong?
<hr>

```{r}
econplot + geom_smooth(aes(color = "Loess, span = .2"), span = .2, se = FALSE) + # used above
  labs(title = "U.S. Unemployment Rate") +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Smoother", values = c("blue")) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
  
```



## What about the abnormalities?
<hr>

Label by day of week

```{r christmas}
christmas <- dfman |> filter(Date >= as.Date("2016-12-20") &
               Date <= ("2017-01-03"))

ggplot(christmas, aes(Date, Gross)) +
    geom_label(aes(label = wday(Date, label = TRUE))) +
    geom_line(color = "cornflowerblue") + 
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b\n%d", date_breaks = "1 day")
```

## Different pattern for Christmas Week
<hr>

Label by day of month

```{r christmas2}
ggplot(christmas, aes(Date, Gross/1000000)) +
    geom_line(color = "cornflowerblue", lwd = 1.1) + 
    geom_point(color = "cornflowerblue", size = 2) +
    geom_label(data = christmas, aes(x = Date, y = Gross/1000000 + .06, 
                   label = day(Date))) +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%a", date_breaks = "1 day") +
    labs(title = "Manchester by the Sea", subtitle = "Christmas Week Box Office Gross",
         x = "Dec 2016 - Jan 2017", y = "Daily Gross (in millions $US)")
```


## Highlight the abnormality
<hr>

```{r}
# annotate Christmas Week
start <- as.Date("2016-12-24")
end <- as.Date("2017-01-02")
g + annotate("rect", xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "green", alpha = .2) +
    annotate("text", x = end + 2, y = 1500000, label = "Dec 24 - Jan 2",
             color = "green", hjust = 0)
```

## Comparisons (multi-line plots)
<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(5702)
tidydf <- data.frame(time = 1:6, y1 = round(rnorm(6, 100, 50), 2),
           y2 = round(rnorm(6, 10, 5), 2)) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = -time)
ggplot(tidydf, aes(time, value, col = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

## Scale the data (create an index)
<hr>

In each group divide by first value, mult by 100


```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| echo: true
head(tidydf, 8)
tidydf_scaled <- tidydf |> group_by(name) |>
  mutate(index = round(100*value/value[1], 2)) |> 
  ungroup()
head(tidydf_scaled, 8)
```


## Comparisons (multi-line plots)
<hr>

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(tidydf, aes(time, value, col = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Original data")

ggplot(tidydf_scaled, aes(time, index, col = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Scaled data")
```

## Discrete data
<hr>

```{r inspection}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
set.seed(5702)
day <- 1:31
number <- 10 * (day - 14)^2 + 2000 + rnorm(1:31, 0, 400)
df <- data.frame(day, number)
ggplot(df, aes(day, number)) +
  geom_line(color = "deeppink") +
  geom_point(color = "deeppink") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:31) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 5000)) +
  labs(title = "Average Motor Vehicle Inspections per Day",
          subtitle = "(fake data)",
       x = "day of month", y = "number of inspections") +
  theme_linedraw(14)
```

## Better for individual values
<hr>

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
ggplot(df, aes(day, number)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:31) +
  labs(title = "Average Motor Vehicle Inspections per Day",
       x = "day of month", y = "number of inspections") +
  theme_linedraw(14)
```

## Gaps
<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: false
# read file
mydat <- read_csv("WA_Sales_Products_2012-14.csv") |> 
  mutate(Revenue = Revenue/1000000)

# convert Quarter to a single numeric value Q
mydat$Q <- as.numeric(substr(mydat$Quarter, 2, 2))

# convert Q to end-of-quarter date
mydat$Date <- as.Date(paste0(mydat$Year, "-",
                             as.character(mydat$Q*3),
                             "-30"))

# Check that dates look ok
# unique(mydat$Date)
```



```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
Methoddata <- mydat |> group_by(Date, `Order method type`) |>
    summarize(Revenue = sum(Revenue))

g <- ggplot(Methoddata, aes(Date, Revenue,
                            color = `Order method type`)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = `Order method type`)) +
    scale_x_date(limits = c(as.Date("2012-02-01"), as.Date("2014-12-31")),
        date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  ylab("Revenue in mil $")
g
```

## Add points to show the frequency of the data
<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
g + geom_point()
```

## Another example
<hr>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
No2013 <- Methoddata |> filter(year(Date) != 2013)
g <- ggplot(No2013, aes(Date, Revenue,
                            color = `Order method type`)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = `Order method type`)) +
    scale_x_date(limits = c(as.Date("2012-02-01"), as.Date("2014-12-31")),
        date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  ylab("Revenue in mil $")
g
```

## Add points to show the frequency of the data
<hr>

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| echo: false
g + geom_point()
```

## Another option: leave gaps
<hr>

Includes dates with missing values and set the value to `NA`

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
Methoddata$Revenue[year(Methoddata$Date)==2013] <- NA
ggplot(Methoddata, aes(Date, Revenue, color = `Order method type`)) + 
    geom_line(aes(group = `Order method type`)) +
    scale_x_date(limits = c(as.Date("2012-02-01"), as.Date("2014-12-31")),
        date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  ylab("Revenue in mil $")
```

## Toy example

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5
df <- data.frame(year = c(2030, 2031, 2032, 2036, 2038), 
                 value = c(100, 110, 140, 180, 185))
ggplot(df, aes(year, value)) + geom_line()

dfgaps <- df |> bind_rows(data.frame(year = c(2033, 2034, 2035), value = c(NA, NA, NA)))
ggplot(dfgaps, aes(year, value)) + geom_line()
```
